newsitem.title: USA: Dow industrials fall after data, NYSE sets curbs.
newsitem.headline: Dow industrials fall after data, NYSE sets curbs.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks declined further, after a weak open on Wednesday, following the release of economic data which showed U.S. factory orders rose 1.2 percent in April. But Nasdaq held steady.
The Dow industrial average was trading down around 35 points at 7276, after its decline prompted the New York Stock Exchange to set curbs on index-arbitrage trading.
The long bond was also weaker, off 14/32 at a 6.91 percent yield. But Nasdaq held relatively firm, up five points at 1390, as technology stocks recovered from yesterday's losses.
"The data was a little bit more than expected, which has thrown the bond market off," Dan Ascani, president and director of research at Global Market Strategies. "But this is a really mixed market."
Factory orders in April rose 1.2 percent compared to a revised decline in March of 1.3 percent.

While blue chip and financial stocks paid more heed to the bond market, technology stocks clawed their way back into positive territory after several profit warnings triggered declines in the sector on Tuesday.
"The market saw sell programs at the get-go but buy programs quickly followed," Guzman trader Tom O'Brien said.
